Island house lots and the s.190.36 rule: Zoning Bylaw s.190.36 provides that no Queensborough (Lulu Island, District Lots 757 and 758) subdivision may produce a lot under one-half acre (0.20 ha) or with frontage under 66 feet (20.12 m) unless the land can connect to the City sanitary sewer system. Most Queensborough lots are sewer-connected, but the connection status of a specific lot governs what can be done with it: not confirmed for any individual lot.

Compact-lot form under the current plan frame: the (RLR) Residential – Low Rise designation in the OCP amendment materials (Bylaw No. 8574, 2026) provides compact-lot single detached form, low-rise buildings up to six storeys, and stacked and side-by-side townhouses, under the Queensborough Community Plan (a schedule to Our City 2041) together with the Queensborough Eastern Neighbourhood Node Master Plan. A designation is a plan position, not a subdivision approval and not a lot offering.

Serviced position: New Westminster operates its own electrical utility and City water / sewer services, and Queensborough drainage is pumped as part of the shared dyking and pumped drainage system with Richmond. A 2026 utility dollar figure for a Queensborough home confirmed on a City source: Not verified. The s.190.36 sewer-connection test above is the parcel-level servicing question that decides subdivision potential here.

ALR vs non-ALR: ALR status for Queensborough: Not verified in the sources read; ALR status for a specific property is checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder. No ALR parcel and no ALR percentage split is stated for this island.

Heritage fabric — built fabric, not offerings: Queensborough properties are documented in the City's Queensborough Residential Heritage Inventory and Queensborough Industrial Heritage Inventory, reflecting the area's historic industrial base — the older streets' lots are existing built fabric, and heritage documentation is a diligence item on a specific lot, not a supply source.

No bare-land strata plan in Queensborough was verified: Stated for the record: a bare-land strata lot is strata tenure (Form B / strata fees / bylaws apply to the lot) — no plan of that form is documented for Queensborough.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Queensborough

items.t: Queensborough is the City of New Westminster's island neighbourhood on the eastern tip of Lulu Island, comprising District Lots 757 and 758 in the Zoning Bylaw wording, bordered by the Fraser River (main arm) to the south and east and the North Arm to the north, and sharing Lulu Island with the City of Richmond. "Queensborough" is the GVR sub-area name as it appears in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report, and the City plans the area through the Queensborough Community Plan, a schedule to the Official Community Plan.

Connection to the rest of the city: Queensborough is joined to mainland New Westminster only by Highway 91A, the Queensborough Connector, over the Queensborough Bridge across the North Arm of the Fraser River to Marine Way / Stewardson Way, with Highway 91 at the south end in Richmond — every trip to Uptown, Downtown or Royal Columbian Hospital crosses that bridge.

Nearby areas: mainland New Westminster (Downtown, Uptown, the Quay) across the Queensborough Bridge to the north-west, Richmond down Lulu Island to the west, Annacis Island (Delta) across the river to the east, and Surrey across the Fraser River main arm to the south.

Roads and transit: Ewen Avenue, Salter Street and Howes Street serve Queensborough; Ewen Avenue is the Main Street commercial strip. No SkyTrain station is in Queensborough; buses connect to 22nd Street Station and New Westminster Station, including TransLink route 104 (Annacis Island / 22nd Street Station, with Port Royal service on weekdays). Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Civic anchors: Ryall Park (sports fields, courts, spray park, community garden, Boro All Wheel Park) sits beside the Queensborough Community Centre, the on-island City recreation facility; Port Royal Park has a riverfront trail; New Westminster Public Library's Queensborough Branch is at 920 Ewen Ave, on the island (Main Branch 716 6th Avenue, mainland); the city's main aquatic centre, the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre, 65 East Sixth Avenue, is on the mainland in Uptown; the nearest hospital is Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street (Fraser Health), on the mainland across the bridge. A named shopping centre owner and address (Queensborough Landing) confirmed on an official source: Not verified.

Schools: SD40 catchments are address-based, and Queensborough is the one New Westminster neighbourhood with its own elementary and middle schools on the island. Queensborough Middle School is at 833 Salter Street. School names are Ministry-listed names, spelled exactly.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Queensborough

items.t: OCP — Our City 2041, Bylaw No. 7925 (2017), with the Queensborough Community Plan as a schedule: the Queensborough Community Plan governs the area together with the Queensborough Eastern Neighbourhood Node Master Plan; the (RLR) Residential – Low Rise designation in the OCP amendment materials (Bylaw No. 8574, 2026) provides compact-lot single detached form, low-rise buildings up to six storeys, and stacked and side-by-side townhouses.

Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 6680 (2001): the Queensborough-specific rule is s.190.36 — no subdivision in District Lots 757 and 758 may produce a lot under one-half acre (0.20 ha) or with frontage under 66 feet (20.12 m) unless the land can connect to the City sanitary sewer system. City-wide, the older townhouse districts are RT-2 through RT-2C plus RT-3/3A/3B (RT-3 is the district recorded for the Jardine Street townhouse site above). The newer RT-A and RT-B districts belong to the City's townhouse program, which its guide says applies to mainland properties, not Queensborough.

Floodplain diligence — THE defining item for Queensborough ground (Zone 1, per the sources): Queensborough is Floodplain Zone 1 in the City's floodplain study: a low-lying area with high groundwater, poor compressible soils and poor drainage, protected by a shared dyking and pumped drainage system with Richmond; the BC dike inventory lists Map 5, New Westminster Queensborough, with the City of New Westminster as diking authority. In the 1960s a perimeter dyke was built protecting approximately 350 hectares; Queensborough has 350 hectares of designated floodplain and is the highest priority for flood protection improvements in the city, and both Queensborough and sections of the mainland are included within the provincial floodplain.

Flood construction levels — the numbers every Queensborough lot is read against: the City's Flood Hazard Development Permit Area sets minimum construction levels of 3.53 metres above Geodetic Survey of Canada datum for Area A (generally downstream from Derwent Way on the south side and Wood Street on the north side) and 4.20 metres above GSC datum for Area B (upstream of Derwent Way and Wood Street) — new buildings in Queensborough should be constructed at an elevation sufficient to minimize loss in the event of dyke failure or an extreme flood topping the perimeter dykes. Confirm the specific lot's area (A or B), its compliance and an insurance quote before subjects come off.

Dike work on the record: the City received $800,000 from the provincial Community Emergency Preparedness Fund for the Queensborough Dike Shoreline Protection Rehabilitation project, restabilising eroding dike slopes at two locations on the northeast side of Lulu Island, behind 345 Gifford Street and behind 805 Boyd Street — for lots near those reaches, confirm the dyke-side position early.

Strata diligence (island strata stock): for strata purchases, review depreciation and contingency under the provincial strata framework early; BC strata disputes can go to the Civil Resolution Tribunal. The full BC strata block applies to any strata lot: Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a "45+" listing line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — Queensborough ALR status is not verified in the sources read): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

Two flood numbers split the island at two streets: Area A (3.53 m GSC) is generally downstream from Derwent Way on the south side and Wood Street on the north side, and Area B (4.20 m GSC) is upstream of those lines — two lots a few blocks apart can carry construction-level requirements 67 centimetres apart, which is a build-cost fact, not a rounding difference.

One bridge is the island's only road link to its own city: every trip to Uptown, Downtown, the aquatic centre or Royal Columbian Hospital crosses the Queensborough Bridge (Highway 91A) — for a land buyer that single connection is both the daily cost and the moat that keeps on-island schools, the community centre and Ryall Park feeling like a small town.

faq.q: Is there a vacant lot subdivision I can buy into in Queensborough?

faq.a: Only through two gates: Zoning Bylaw s.190.36 bars a new lot under one-half acre (0.20 ha) or under 66 feet (20.12 m) of frontage unless the land can connect to the City sanitary sewer system, and subdivision approval itself runs under Subdivision and Development Control Bylaw No. 7142, 2007 (Approving Officer approval, full works-and-services standard, Zoning Bylaw minimums, OCP consistency). The specific lot's sewer-connection status is the deciding fact — not verified until checked.
faq.q: Can I split my Queensborough lot?

faq.a: The Flood Hazard Development Permit Area minimums: 3.53 metres above GSC datum in Area A (generally downstream from Derwent Way / Wood Street) and 4.20 metres above GSC datum in Area B (upstream). Pull the lot's area, its flood construction level compliance and an insurance quote before subjects come off.
faq.q: What elevation does a new build on my lot have to meet?

faq.a: A Portside purchase runs on a Form B, not a disclosure statement, and it is a strata purchase, not a lot purchase.

faq.a: By Highway 91A, the Queensborough Connector, over the Queensborough Bridge across the North Arm of the Fraser River to Marine Way / Stewardson Way; Highway 91 connects at the south end in Richmond.
faq.q: How does Queensborough connect to the rest of New Westminster?

faq.a: Yes — it is Floodplain Zone 1 in the City's study, a low-lying area with high groundwater and poor drainage protected by a perimeter dyke built in the 1960s covering about 350 hectares and a pumped drainage system shared with Richmond; new construction must meet flood construction levels of 3.53 m (Area A) or 4.20 m (Area B) above GSC datum.
